annotation.title_clean: Canadian Jurisdictional Guidelines for the Safe Testing and Deployment of Vehicles Equipped with Automated Driving Systems, Version 2.0
annotation.title_en: Canadian Jurisdictional Guidelines for the Safe Testing and Deployment of Vehicles Equipped with Automated Driving Systems, Version 2.0
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Canadian Council of Motor Transport Administrators (CCMTA)
annotation.summary_en: Voluntary CCMTA guidelines (2nd edition, Feb 2022) advising Canadian provinces and territories on testing and deploying SAE Level 3–5 automated driving system vehicles. They cover permits, registration, insurance, driver licensing, law enforcement, incident reporting, cybersecurity, data, shuttles, delivery devices, connected vehicles and truck platooning, balancing road safety with innovation.
key_provisions_or_claims: Establish an ADS Committee and lead agency in each jurisdiction to coordinate testing and deployment policy.
Require vehicle-specific test permits with safety assessment, ODD, safety plan and at least $5M liability insurance.
Flag ADS Level on registration records; deployed vehicles must meet CMVSS unless exempted by Transport Canada.
Clearly establish legal responsibility; registered owner responsible for Level 4/5 vehicles; collision reporting within 24 hours.
Remote test drivers must be in-jurisdiction, licensed and drive one vehicle at a time; micro utility/delivery devices use municipal opt-in, no full deployment yet.
